t: #3569 Maximize Count of Distinct Primes After Split
o: For each update we must output max over splits k of (distinct primes in prefix) + (distinct primes in suffix). A prime value v contributes to the prefix iff it occurs at some position < k, i.e. k > minPos(v); it contributes to the suffix iff maxPos(v) >= k. So f(k) = #{v : minPos(v) < k} + #{v : maxPos(v) >= k}, and we need max f(k) for k in [1, n-1]. An update changes the min/max position of at most two values, each changing f(k) on a contiguous range by +-1. Constraints (n, q <= 5e4, values <= 1e5) point to a lazy segment tree with range-add and global-max, plus per-value min/max occurrence tracking.
k: f(k) = #primes with minPos < k + #primes with maxPos >= k; only min/max positions of each value matter.
Each point update triggers O(1) range-add updates on f, so a lazy segment tree with global max suffices.
Track per-value min/max positions with heaps + lazy deletion (a 'removed' flag per index).

a.n: Approach 1: Lazy Segment Tree over split points
a.i: Build f(k) initially from each prime value's min/max occurrence. On updating index idx from ov to val, mark idx removed, subtract the old-extent ranges of ov, insert idx into val's structures, unmark, add the new-extent ranges of val. The segment tree maintains range add and global max, which is the answer.
s: For each value keep a min-heap and max-heap of positions with lazy deletion via a removed[] flag.
Define add(v, sign): if v occurs, range-add sign on [minPos+1, n-1] and [1, maxPos].
Apply initial contributions; per query apply removal/addition contributions and output the tree's global max.
a.t: O((n + q) log n) — each update does O(1) segment-tree range updates; heap operations amortized O(log n).
a.sp: O(n + V) for heaps, flags, and the segment tree.

w: The key leap is rewriting the objective purely in terms of each value's min/max occurrence positions, turning a seemingly quadratic 'try every split' problem into range additions. Pitfalls: forgetting the primality filter, handling a value that disappears entirely (its two ranges vanish), and stale heap entries after re-insertion. Follow-up: what if we needed the minimizing split k too (store argmax in the tree).
